Over 40,000 New Jersey residents lost power as storms rolled through, while quarter-sized hail and damaging winds affected multiple counties, and lightning caused a weather delay at Nissan Stadium in Tennessee. A Next Weather Alert was in effect for the Philadelphia region due to the combination of heat and heavy storms.

incidents.summary: Two weeks after the earthquake, over 6,000 evacuees remain in shelters, with preparations underway to move them to hotels. The Japanese government will apply reconstruction aid law to all of Kumamoto Prefecture, offering up to ¥3 million for housing repair, while U.S. Forces airlifted 33,000 bottles of drinking water to the region. Additional aftermath reports include a fireworks display honoring victims, a survivor urging youth to pursue peace, and warnings about post-quake scams and crimes targeting damaged homes and shelters.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary: New updates include the death of an elderly woman from heat stroke while sheltering in her car, bringing indirect tolls into focus. news.body: Officials say the latest victim from a powerful earthquake that struck Japan’s southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto last week is an elderly woman who apparently developed heat stroke while taking shelter in a car. The fatality came as concerns of heat-related illness grow in the area that is also suffering extreme temperatures. The magnitude 7.1 quake hit Kumamoto on Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu on Tuesday. The death toll is now 36. Authorities have ended a massive search-and-rescue operation at a collapsed shopping mall in southwest Japan after retrieving five people and the bodies of seven others over the past five days.

logs.summary: Two weeks after the earthquake, over 6,000 evacuees remain in shelters, with preparations underway to move them to hotels. The Japanese government will apply reconstruction aid law to all of Kumamoto Prefecture, offering up to ¥3 million for housing repair, while U.S. Forces airlifted 33,000 bottles of drinking water to the region. Additional aftermath reports include a fireworks display honoring victims, a survivor urging youth to pursue peace, and warnings about post-quake scams and crimes targeting damaged homes and shelters.

news.body: Residents of Japan’s quake-hit southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto are working to clear their homes in intense heat, as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi briefly visited Kumamoto Prefecture on Monday for the first time since a magnitude 7.1 quake last Tuesday. The heat and a lack of water have added to the challenges in the severely damaged areas. The quake killed 38 people, including one who died of apparent heat stroke while taking shelter in a car in hot weather. Residents put out heaps of debris, broken furniture and damaged appliances for collection, while in the towns of Uki and Hikawa, construction of temporary housing began.
